subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters now, or defer this issue to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The source-level hot path is clear, but the permanent boundary affects provider hooks, plugin metadata lifecycle, custom providers, and the prepared-runtime direction.

options.title: Land the bounded cache
options.body: Refresh or land the open cache PR with conservative invalidation and proof that custom provider hooks and fresh execute closures still bypass stale cached data.

options.title: Fold into prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader prepared-runtime rollout removes the repeated provider/tool normalization work without a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Wait for current-main live Google/Gemini or heap evidence before approving the cache direction, accepting that the source-level repeated work remains open meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Land the bounded cache
recommendation.body: Refresh or land the open cache PR with conservative invalidation and proof that custom provider hooks and fresh execute closures still bypass stale cached data.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision intersects the prepared-runtime tracker and cache-boundary architecture most directly.
